hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.
note: seeds best-so-far and the convergence window; does not start the stall counter

hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise FM with LightGBM trained with lambdarank over ~6-row chronological user groups, on base5 plus out-of-fold item/author long-view rates, will beat the 0.6016 baseline by a wide margin.
rationale: Three structural mismatches are fixed at once on the axes the harness declares exempt plus the single strongest feature block: (a) the loss becomes a ranking loss whose gradient is the NDCG swap gain, matching the metric; (b) training groups are capped at 6 consecutive rows so the list length the pairwise discount sees matches the ~5.6-row valid lists rather than 43.5-row train lists; (c) an OOF item long-view rate gives the model an explicit, within-user-varying quality signal that a pointwise FM can only reach indirectly through a video_id embedding trained on ~1 exposure per (u,v) pair. Trees also handle a mixed numeric/categorical frame, which FM cannot.
expected_gain_derivation: [POINTWISE_BASELINE] plus [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH] plus [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] all point at the same untouched axis; the organizers exhausted feature width and capacity ([ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD],[ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD]) without ever changing the loss, so the residual headroom is concentrated here. Baseline 0.6016 against a [CEILING] of 0.8484 leaves 0.247 of range; item-rate + ranking loss typically recovers 10-20% of such a gap in logged-impression reranking, i.e. +0.025 to +0.05. [HIGH_COVERAGE] (99.9% of valid videos in train) means the OOF item rates are populated for nearly every valid row, so I take the middle of that band: +0.035.

block_justifications.base5: These are the exact fields the 0.6016 baseline uses and the organizers state the user_id x video_id interaction absorbs most learnable signal, so dropping them would confound a loss-function test with a feature ablation.
block_justifications.item_agg: Video/author long-view and click rates differ across the items inside one user's list, so unlike user-side aggregates they can actually reorder that list [WITHIN_USER_RANKING], and [HIGH_COVERAGE] guarantees 99.9% of valid videos have a train-window rate.

hypothesis: Adding explicit duration features (log duration and within-user duration percentile) to the iteration-1 LightGBM lambdarank spec will produce the largest single jump, because the long_view label is defined by a watch-time threshold that interacts directly with video length.
rationale: On KuaiRand long_view is a play-time threshold judged against the video's own duration, so P(long_view) is close to a monotone function of duration; base5 only exposes a coarse, user-independent dur_bucket. dur_feats adds continuous log-duration resolution plus the duration percentile computed WITHIN the user's own list, which is exactly the kind of quantity that reorders a 6-item list and is immune to being constant per user. It is also drift-safe: a within-list percentile is uniform on [0,1] regardless of whether the list has 43 rows or 6.
expected_gain_derivation: [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED] names duration-bias modelling as untouched, and [WITHIN_USER_RANKING]/[SHORT_EVAL_LISTS] mean a feature that varies smoothly across the ~6 items of a list is the only kind that can move nDCG@5. Iteration 1 (base5+item_agg, same objective/grouping) sat at 0.60208 with primary_std 0.00057, so this spec is a clean one-block delta against it. Distance to [CEILING] 0.8484 is 0.246; I credit a genuine label-mechanics feature with ~6% of that remaining gap, i.e. +0.015, well outside [SEED_NOISE] 0.0008.

hypothesis: Adding cross_agg (user x author affinity, user x tag affinity, duration relative to the user's own historically long-viewed duration) and switching to a listwise rank_xendcg loss over 6-row chronological groups will produce the first real jump, because it is the first feature block that encodes user-item MATCH rather than item quality, and listwise softmax over a 6-item group is the closest available training analogue of ordering a whole ~6-item valid list.
rationale: Item popularity rates and duration are item-side quantities: within one user's short list they mostly reproduce a global preference order, which is why iterations 1 and 2 moved the metric by less than seed noise. The organizers state that the user_id x video_id interaction absorbs most of the learnable signal, and a GBDT cannot construct that interaction from two high-cardinality categoricals -- it needs the interaction handed to it numerically. cross_agg is exactly that: affinity terms that differ between the items in one user's list and are therefore capable of reordering it. Pairing it with rank_xendcg removes the position discount, which is the right geometry when nDCG@5 over ~6 items is effectively whole-list ordering.
expected_gain_derivation: [ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD] and [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD] say item-side and static information is exhausted, while the organizers' own diagnosis attributes the working signal to the user x item interaction; cross_agg is the only untried block supplying that in a form that varies within a list [WITHIN_USER_RANKING], unlike user_agg which is provably inert [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT]. The FM's whole edge over a popularity ranker comes from that interaction, so recovering it inside a tree model plausibly recovers a similar magnitude; against a 0.6021 base and a 0.8484 ceiling [CEILING] I put that at ~0.010, roughly 12x seed noise [SEED_NOISE], while acknowledging the two prior structural moves each returned under 0.001.
